$schema: hand-maintained curated dependency/license ledger — see docs/legal/RELEASE-SAFEGUARDS.md
_comment: Same convention as scripts/arch-metrics/budgets.json and inference/catalog/models.json: derived from real, checkable evidence at the time it was written (license text in the local Go module cache, or package.json 'license' field for baked npm packages), then hand-maintained going forward. scripts/check-third-party-notices.sh re-derives the LIVE dependency set at gate time and fails closed if it diverges from this ledger IN EITHER DIRECTION (a new dep with no entry, an entry whose class the policy disallows, or a ledger row that is no longer in the live build graph — stale attribution).

goModules.notes: File-level weak copyleft. Linked into pix-host in Executable Form via an unmodified Go module import — pix creates no Modifications (MPL-2.0 s1.10), so the only Source Code Form a recipient needs is the upstream one linked above, at the pinned version. Attribution per MPL-2.0 s3.3 is this entry plus the verbatim license text shipped at licenses/MPL-2.0.txt.
Same MPL-2.0 posture as go-plugin (yamux is go-plugin's multiplexed-stream transport): unmodified import, no Modifications distributed.

Transitive dependency of modernc.org/libc (used by modernc.org/sqlite). Platform-gated: only reachable on darwin/windows builds (the cross-compiled darwin/amd64 + darwin/arm64 release targets per publish.yml), invisible to a linux-only `go list -deps` — see scripts/legal/list-go-modules.sh. LICENSE verified in the module cache at v1.0.0: standard MIT text, copyright 2022 Nuno Cruces. Source: https://github.com/ncruces/go-strftime
Supervision-tree library for the host `serve` supervisor (services/host/supervise). LICENSE verified at v4.0.6 in the module cache: standard MIT text, copyright 2014-2024 Barracuda Networks, Inc.
Dual-licensed: LICENSE is Apache-2.0; NOTICE/portions under MIT (apache-license.txt / MIT-LICENSE.txt upstream). Treated as permissive.

bakedTools.name: ruff
bakedTools.role: Dockerfile: official static binary release, fetched via `curl` from GitHub Releases (pinned by ARG RUFF_VERSION, not `releases/latest`), installed to /usr/local/bin/ruff — Python lint/format toolchain for agent use.
bakedTools.licenseEvidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astral-sh/ruff/0.15.22/LICENSE — live-fetched at the exact pinned tag; MIT, copyright Charles Marsh. That file also reproduces third-party MIT-licensed code ruff embeds (autoflake, Flake8, isort, Pyright, pyupgrade, etc.) as attribution notices within ruff's own LICENSE — all MIT, no additional obligations beyond ruff's own.

bakedTools.name: fd
bakedTools.role: Dockerfile: official static binary release, fetched via `curl` from GitHub Releases (pinned by ARG FD_VERSION), installed to /usr/local/bin/fd and symlinked into ~/.pi/agent/bin/fd — fast file finder pi otherwise auto-downloads per-sandbox.
bakedTools.licenseEvidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sharkdp/fd/v10.4.2/LICENSE-MIT and .../LICENSE-APACHE — both live-fetched at the exact pinned tag. Dual-licensed (recipient's choice of either); treated as permissive, notices elect the MIT text.

bakedTools.name: go
bakedTools.role: Dockerfile: official Go toolchain tarball, fetched via `curl` from go.dev/dl (pinned by ARG GO_VERSION to match services/host/go.mod's `go` directive), installed to /usr/local/go — builds/tests the host binary (pix-host) from inside a sandbox. Distributed as a runtime/compiler in the image, not imported source, but still a directly-downloaded bundled binary.
bakedTools.licenseEvidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/golang/go/go1.26.5/LICENSE — live-fetched at the exact pinned tag; BSD-3-Clause, copyright The Go Authors. Same license class already carried by the golang.org/x/* modules above.

npmGlobal.name: @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent
npmGlobal.role: npm install -g (Dockerfile ARG PI_PACKAGE) — the pi CLI itself

npmGlobal.name: @earendil-works/pi-tui
npmGlobal.author: Mario Zechner
npmGlobal.role: transitive dependency of pi-coding-agent; PATCHED at image build time by scripts/patches/apply-tui-bottom-pin.mjs (see docs/upstream/tui-bottom-pin.md). The patch is a narrow, reviewable, idempotent modification to the installed dist/tui.js, not a fork or redistribution of modified source under a different name.
